ideas.hypothesis: The underinvestment caused by information asymmetry is concentrated in firms with large growth opportunities: the sensitivity of investment to internal cash flow rises with measured information asymmetry (bid-ask spread) more steeply for high market-to-book firms than for low market-to-book firms.

sources.role: mechanism: dynamic model predicting that undervaluation of growth opportunities under information asymmetry distorts investment most for high-growth firms
mechanism: Myers-Majluf adverse selection in security issuance and its link to financing choices
measure: spread-based estimator of information asymmetry (Venkatesh and Chiang) for listed firms

ideas.test: Use a panel of listed non-financial firms in one market (e.g., Tehran or Amman, 8-10 years) with annual capital expenditure, operating cash flow, market-to-book, and daily bid-ask quotes. Estimate investment on cash flow, spread, market-to-book, and their triple interaction with firm and year fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: The triple interaction is zero or negative: cash-flow sensitivity of investment does not increase more with information asymmetry in high-growth firms than in low-growth firms.

ideas.hypothesis: The negative effect of information asymmetry on dividend payouts is weaker in firms with concentrated ownership, because a dominant shareholder's monitoring substitutes for dividends as a signal or as a tool for controlling agency costs.

sources.role: finding and setting: information asymmetry affects dividend policy among Amman-listed firms, alongside size and profitability
measure and setting: joint analysis of information asymmetry, ownership concentration and dividends on Tehran Stock Exchange

ideas.test: Using 6-8 years of data for all firms listed on one exchange, regress payout ratio (or a probability-of-paying model) on spread-based information asymmetry, largest-shareholder stake, and their interaction, controlling for size, profitability, and book-to-market, with industry and year fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: The interaction is insignificant or has the opposite sign, so information asymmetry reduces dividends equally (or more) in firms with concentrated ownership.

ideas.hypothesis: Periodic financial statement disclosure narrows bid-ask spreads among listed banks, and the narrowing is larger and lasts longer for banks with low trading volume, where private information is otherwise slow to be priced.

sources.role: setting and measure: Jordanian commercial banks with daily best-bid/best-offer spreads around periodic disclosure, with trading volume as covariate
measure: spread-based information asymmetry and floating stock turnover

ideas.test: Event study around quarterly and annual report release dates for all banks listed on Amman Stock Exchange over 3-5 years: compute abnormal spreads in windows [-10,-1], [0,+5], [+6,+20] relative to a baseline, and interact the post-disclosure change with pre-period average trading volume terciles.
ideas.disconfirming: Spreads do not narrow after disclosure, or the post-disclosure narrowing is no larger for low-volume banks than for high-volume banks.

ideas.hypothesis: Individuals with higher measured loss aversion show a larger positive bias when interpreting ambiguous news about assets they previously favored while those assets are in a loss, which explains the asymmetric belief persistence seen in investment experiments.

sources.role: finding and method: investment experiment showing biased perception of new information for favored assets that is stronger under losses than gains
method: experimental simulation of investor information use and performance

ideas.test: Lab experiment with about 150 participants: elicit each person's loss aversion with mixed-gamble choices, then run a multi-period portfolio task in which signals of fixed objective informativeness arrive about chosen and unchosen assets in gain and loss states; measure posterior beliefs and trades. Regress belief-updating bias on loss aversion interacted with gain/loss state and asset preference.
ideas.disconfirming: Belief-updating bias toward favored assets under losses is unrelated to individual loss-aversion coefficients.

ideas.hypothesis: Training novice investors to follow the information-access sequence used by better-performing analysts improves their portfolio returns more when the number of available information cues is large, because the strategy chiefly reduces the costs of information overload.

sources.role: finding and method: training novices in analysts' information-accessing strategies improved performance, even during a market downturn
mechanism: biased processing of new information by investors

ideas.test: 2x2 between-subjects experiment (training vs no training; 8 vs 30 available information items per stock) in a simulated trading task using historical stock data; outcome is risk-adjusted portfolio return and decision time, analyzed with a two-way ANOVA.
ideas.disconfirming: The training effect on returns is the same size (or smaller) in the high-cue condition as in the low-cue condition, or training has no effect at all.

ideas.hypothesis: Displaying real-time travel-time savings next to the toll price on variable message signs increases managed-lane use at a given toll, and makes lane choice more responsive to actual congestion, compared with displaying price alone.

sources.role: finding and mechanism: managed-lane users' information needs, sign comprehension, and a driver decision-making model from focus groups
finding: most commuters rely on radio, TV and changeable message signs rather than advanced systems
method: attributes and methods for valuing transport information

ideas.test: Partner with a managed-lane operator to alternate sign content (price only vs price plus estimated minutes saved) by day over 8-12 weeks; use toll-tag transactions and loop-detector speeds to estimate lane-choice probability as a function of toll, actual time savings, and message type.
ideas.disconfirming: Managed-lane share and its sensitivity to actual time savings are the same on days with time-savings messages as on price-only days.

ideas.hypothesis: Valuations that lean more on soft, judgment-based information (fewer comparable transactions, more valuer adjustments) show larger absolute deviations from later transaction prices and greater dispersion across valuers, especially in thin markets.

sources.role: mechanism: intangible elements of uncertainty and risk in valuation beyond tangible methods
setting: housing market where buyers face hard-to-evaluate pricing of scheme-backed purchases

ideas.test: Obtain a sample of 500-1,000 valuation reports linked to subsequent sale prices from one lender or valuation firm; code the number of comparables used and the size of qualitative adjustments. Regress absolute valuation error on these soft-information indicators with location and time fixed effects, interacting with local transaction volume.
ideas.disconfirming: Valuation error and dispersion do not rise with the share of judgment-based adjustments or with sparse comparables.

ideas.hypothesis: For startups offering new products in new markets, investor due diligence that assesses founders' effectual behaviors (using available means, affordable loss, pre-commitments from partners) predicts startup survival and follow-on funding better than due diligence focused on business-plan forecasts.

sources.role: mechanism: understanding effectuation could improve due diligence of start-ups offering new products in new markets
mechanism: growth opportunities are hard for outsiders to value under information asymmetry

ideas.test: Code due-diligence memos from an angel network or accelerator (about 200 deals) for effectual vs predictive assessment criteria; link to 3-5 year outcomes (survival, follow-on round). Estimate logit models of outcomes on criteria scores, separately for new-market vs existing-market ventures.
ideas.disconfirming: Effectuation-based scores do not predict outcomes beyond predictive criteria, or predict equally well in existing markets.

ideas.hypothesis: The value of real-time traffic and terminal-queue information to drayage truck operators rises with travel-time variability, so fleets receiving such information reduce turn times and unproductive miles more on corridors and days with high variability.

sources.role: setting and method: South Florida FRATIS demonstration plan with hypotheses, testing protocols and data elements
setting: LA-Gateway FRATIS prototype and small-scale demonstrations
method: attributes affecting the value of transport information and valuation approaches

ideas.test: Use GPS and dispatch logs from participating and non-participating drayage fleets during a FRATIS-type demonstration; estimate difference-in-differences in terminal turn time and empty miles, interacted with daily corridor travel-time variability from probe data.
ideas.disconfirming: Information-receiving fleets show no greater improvement than controls on high-variability days than on low-variability days.

ideas.hypothesis: Aggregating expert rankings with the Borda count, which uses each judge's full ranking, yields consensus rankings of vintage quality that predict later market prices and expert scores better than Condorcet-based aggregation.

sources.role: method: Borda count versus Condorcet method for aggregating rankings, and the information each discards
mechanism: individual priors bias how information is perceived, motivating robust aggregation

ideas.test: Collect published expert rankings of vintages for one wine region over 20-30 years; compute Borda and Condorcet (e.g., Kemeny) consensus rankings using leave-one-year-out samples; compare rank correlations of each with later auction prices or retrospective expert ratings.
ideas.disconfirming: Condorcet-based rankings predict later prices as well as or better than Borda rankings.
